text:
GENERATE BURST KP-B1d — SECOND style/proof image of the Crucible arena: the chancel of a militant faith's cathedral, sacked THIS WEEK, painted at plate scale over a geometry guide + an authored DAMAGE MAP (Run KC2-PLAY, Wave 2; conductor gandalf; Matt: "obscenely beautiful — a scene you can't take your eyes away from, and a place you would never want to be"). task_id "KP-B1d". Supersedes KP-B1a as the style pass (Matt: the style was right; the building's identity and its damage were wrong).

WHAT THIS IS. One painted ground-plate chunk, 1536x1024, for a hand-painted 2D action RPG arena. Camera fixed at 52.95 degrees down (elevated three-quarter), screen-up is NORTH. Scale is exact: 1 m EAST = 100.6 px across; 1 m SOUTH = 80.3 px down. The chunk is 15.3 m x 12.8 m of floor: the NORTH END of the nave (the chancel), the gate/origin at pixel (768, 799). A 1.9 m player = 115 px tall stands on this floor (IMAGE 3). Everything painted must be sized to that figure.

THE BUILDING (identity — describe, never name): a fortress-cathedral of a crusading order that held a border against hell and lost it. MASS before grace: enormous piers, Romanesque weight with gothic verticals, cold GREY-WHITE and BLACK dressed stone, IRON everywhere (bound doors, grilles over the side chapels, chains from the vault, iron-strapped reliquaries, braziers). Its faith is a faith of the SUN and the CHAIN: a great gold SUN-DISC behind the altar where a rose window would be, the order's sigil a chained sun, saints carved as armoured knights, candles by the thousand with wax run down the stone, red-and-white banners, relic bones in glass. Its surfaces are SMOOTH and BEAUTIFUL — polished by centuries of feet and knees and wax — because this building was WHOLE a week ago. IMAGE 4 is the same building seen from outside, burning: match its stone and its fire.

THE BATTLE THAT MADE THIS ROOM (the floor must let a player READ it; IMAGE 6 is the map, IMAGE 7 the mask):
 E1 — a demon-gate opened AT the gate (768, 799): a CRATER of broken flagstones (magenta), a spall ring around it, ELEVEN radial cracks running outward and dying within 2-4 m (white lines — these are the only long cracks on the floor), black blast-scorch, and EJECTA thrown NORTH up the dais steps (blue dots): stone chunks, a bent iron grille, one candle-tree flung and burning.
 E2 — a FIRE started in the choir stalls on the EAST side (orange ring): the stalls are charred skeletons, wax has melted and run, the flagstones there are SCORCHED BLACK BUT NOT CRACKED, and a V-shaped SOOT PLUME climbs the east wall above where it started (grey V), opening upward.
 E3 — the apse's NORTH-EAST PIER FAILED (blue cone): the vault above it fell in a wedge; a talus cone of vault blocks and ribs lies at the angle of repose; EACH fallen block cracked ONLY the tile it landed on — one short fracture or a tiny 2-3-ray star UNDER the block (yellow), nowhere else. The pier is crushed at its base and leans.
 E4 — the WEST wall was BREACHED FROM OUTSIDE by siege (magenta bar): stone thrown INWARD in a fan (blue), biggest nearest the wall; the hole's edges are jagged along the stone coursing; the SUNSET floods in through it.
 THE CRACK LAW — this is a hard rule and the reason this image exists: cracks appear ONLY where IMAGE 6/7 draw them (white radials, yellow impact marks). EVERY OTHER TILE AND EVERY OTHER STONE SURFACE IS SMOOTH AND WHOLE — no spiderweb cracks, no crazing, no all-over fracture texture, no "aged ruin" treatment. Real dressed stone fails along its joints and only under a load; a battle leaves DIRECTION (radials from a blast, a fan from a breach, a cone under a fall, a V above a fire), age leaves webs, and this is a battle. Fresh cracks are clean-edged and pale inside with grit beside them. Damage is local and legible; the untouched 80 % of the floor is beautiful.

THE DESECRATION (the horror is what hell did to the beautiful thing; readable at small size, no gore-as-texture): the sun-disc has been torn from the apse and lies half-buried in the crater's ejecta, its gold face up; on the apse wall where it hung, a knight-saint of the order hangs on chains, arms fixed wide, fire glowing through the arch behind him; the altar is overturned and blood runs from it down the dais steps in the floor's low places; the flagstones between the piers carry ritual marks cut fresh into the stone; skin-banners hang over the order's red-and-white banners; bone heaps against the east wall in the shape of a pyre; candles still burning among all of it. Pools of burning pitch seep up through the broken flagstones at the crater and the breach — pitch poured over something.

LIGHT: the sun sets in the WEST (screen LEFT); through the west breach the sunset floods in — long GOLD shafts rake EAST across the polished floor between the piers, piers throwing long violet-blue shadows; ash falls through the shafts. Fire (crater, pitch, the arch behind the hanging knight, candles) is the ONLY saturated warm; the sunset is gold-amber and diffuse; everything else is deep cool violet-blue with readable shadows, never pure black. Beauty and horror in the same light.

REGISTER (frozen): HAND-DRAWN painted 2D as in IMAGE 5 (our own cliffside level): confident dark contour with visible taper and varying weight, painted fills in clean planes, restrained texture, readable silhouettes, no conspicuous brush or pixel grain; not pixel art, not cel-shaded, not a 3D render, not photoreal. Match IMAGE 5's hand exactly; only the building and its light differ. No text, no UI, no figures, no grid.

THE OUTSIDE: everything that is not inside the nave — beyond the apse wall, beyond the side walls, through the breach — is flat pure #00ff00 exactly (no gradient, no haze, no smoke over it). Wall faces may rise up-screen from their footprints; where the world ends, the pixel is #00ff00.

DELIVER exactly ONE 1536x1024 image_gen result in EDIT mode over IMAGE 1 (the scale-true floor guide; IMAGE 2 is the grid/suggested-boundary annotation, information only). ONE retry only if: spiderweb/all-over cracks appear on surfaces the map leaves whole, the outside is not flat #00ff00, the register drifts from IMAGE 5, the scale is wrong against IMAGE 3, or the four events cannot be read — name the reason. Copy the output from $CODEX_HOME/generated_images/... to out/b1d_nave_01.png with sha256. No code. No other files. No web.
RETURN: receipt task_id "KP-B1d"; images = the file with prompt, references and elapsed_s; calls_used = the TRUE number of image_gen calls; status DELIVERED / DELIVERED_WITH_CONCERNS / FAILED; concerns listed honestly. Never PASS/FAIL.

references.role: IMAGE 1 — scale-true floor guide to EDIT (1536x1024)
IMAGE 2 — annotation: 1 m grid, suggested boundary + gate, origin cross (information only)
IMAGE 3 — scale figure: the player at 115 px = 1.9 m (do not paint)
IMAGE 4 — the same cathedral seen from outside, burning (identity + stone + fire)
IMAGE 5 — register exemplar: our painted cliffside level (match the hand exactly)
IMAGE 6 — the DAMAGE MAP over the guide: E1 blast radials + crater + ejecta, E2 fire scorch + soot V, E3 pier-fall talus + impact marks, E4 west breach fan (cracks ONLY where drawn)
IMAGE 7 — the damage MASK (class colours; black = untouched, smooth, whole)
